title: Judges 18
paragraphs: ¹ In those days there was no king in Israel. The tribe of Dan was still looking for a territory of their own to settle, because they had not yet received their full share among the tribes of Israel. ² The Danites sent five warriors from their clans, from Zorah and Eshtaol, to scout the land and explore it. They were told, "Go and explore." When they reached the hill country of Ephraim, they came to Micah's house and spent the night there. ³ While staying at Micah's house, they recognized the voice of the young Levite. They went in and asked him, "How did you end up here? What are you doing in this place? What's your work here?" ⁴ He told them what Micah had arranged with him — that he had hired him to be his priest. ⁵ They asked him, "Please inquire of God for us, so we can know whether our mission will succeed."

⁶ The priest said to them, "Go in peace. Your journey has the LORD's blessing." ⁷ The five men set out and arrived at Laish. They saw that the people there lived in safety, like the Sidonians — peaceful and secure. No one in the region had the authority to oppress them in any way. They were far from Sidon and had no ties to anyone else. ⁸ The scouts returned to their kinsmen at Zorah and Eshtaol, who asked, "What's your report?" ⁹ They said, "Get moving — let's attack them! We've seen the land, and it's excellent. Are you just going to sit here? Don't hesitate — go and take possession of it. ¹⁰ When you arrive, you'll find an unsuspecting people in a spacious land. God has given it into your hands — a place that lacks nothing the earth has to offer."

¹¹ Six hundred Danite warriors, armed for battle, set out from Zorah and Eshtaol. ¹² They camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah — that place is still called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it lies west of Kiriath-jearim. ¹³ From there they moved on through the hill country of Ephraim and came to Micah's house. ¹⁴ The five men who had spied out the region around Laish spoke up to their kinsmen: "Do you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household idols, a carved image, and a cast idol? Think about what you want to do." ¹⁵ They turned toward the house and went to the home of the young Levite — Micah's house — and greeted him.

¹⁶ The six hundred armed Danite warriors stood guard at the entrance of the gate, ¹⁷ while the five scouts went in and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol. The priest stood at the gate with the six hundred armed men. ¹⁸ When the scouts went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household idols, and the cast idol, the priest said, "What are you doing?" ¹⁹ They told him, "Be quiet. Keep your mouth shut and come with us. Be our father and priest — is it better to be priest for one man's house, or priest for a whole tribe and clan in Israel?" ²⁰ The priest was glad. He took the ephod, the household idols, and the carved image and went along with the people.

²¹ They set out with the children, the livestock, and the valuables leading the way. ²² When they had gone some distance from Micah's house, his neighbors came together and caught up with the Danites. ²³ They called out to them, and the Danites turned and said to Micah, "What's the matter with you that you've come after us with this mob?" ²⁴ He said, "You took my gods that I made, and the priest — you've gone off with everything. What do I have left? How can you say 'What's the matter with you?'" ²⁵ The Danites replied, "Don't raise your voice against us, or some hot-tempered men will come at you and cost you your life and the lives of your household."

²⁶ So the Danites went on their way. Micah, seeing that they were too strong for him, turned around and went home. ²⁷ They took what Micah had made, along with his priest, and attacked Laish — a peaceful, unsuspecting people. They killed them with the sword and burned down the city. ²⁸ There was no one to rescue them, for Laish was far from Sidon and had no alliance with anyone. It lay in the valley near Beth-rehob. They rebuilt the city and settled there. ²⁹ They named it Dan after their ancestor Dan, a son of Israel — though the city had originally been called Laish. ³⁰ The Danites set up the carved image, and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, along with his sons, served as priests to the tribe of Dan until the time of the exile.
³¹ They kept Micah's carved image in place throughout the entire time the house of God was at Shiloh.
